title: How To make Some Text In a whatsapp message as link
author: Stefan Bogdanescu

content: # Why WhatsApp Doesn't Support Inline Links and What You Can Do Instead You might be used to seeing hyperlinks embedded directly within text on web platforms or in email clients, where clicking a word like "Click here" takes you to a destination URL. However, the architecture of WhatsApp is fundamentally different from these environments. The platform treats standard text messages as plain data packets rather than rendered HTML documents. Consequently, there is no native API or setting that allows you to format specific words within a message body into clickable links. The behavior you are looking forâwhere a specific string of text turns blue, underlines itself upon hovering (or long-pressing), and functions as a hyperlinkâis technically an "inline link." WhatsApp deliberately disables this feature to maintain consistency in how messages are displayed across different devices. Whether you are on an Android phone with a stock launcher or an iPhone using the native messaging app, the rendering engine strips out HTML tags meant to create these inline styles. If you paste code containing `text` into a WhatsApp chat, the tags are ignored, and the text appears as plain characters. This limitation often leads developers and content creators to look for workarounds, hoping to find a hidden configuration or a third-party library that can inject this functionality via an API. Unfortunately, because WhatsApp operates on a strict client-server model where the server-side rendering logic dictates what the user sees, there is no backend method to force a specific text segment to behave as a link without changing the entire message structure. The blue color you see in screenshots of other apps indicates that those platforms are parsing Markdown or HTML and applying CSS classes accordingly. WhatsApp simply does not perform this parsing for standard messages. However, if your goal is to allow users to copy a specific piece of text rather than the entire message, you can achieve this by leveraging the platform's native link behavior in a slightly different way. Since direct inline formatting is impossible, the most reliable method is to send the URL as a separate message immediately following the descriptive text. When a user long-presses a valid URL in WhatsApp, they are presented with an option to "Copy Link Address." This effectively isolates the copyable action from the rest of the conversational text, mimicking the utility you originally sought without requiring unsupported formatting features. For developers building integrations using the WhatsApp Business API, the constraints remain similar regarding message content. The API accepts JSON payloads for text and media, but it does not provide a parameter to define link attributes within a string field. The `text` field must be treated as plain UTF-8 characters. If you attempt to inject HTML entities or Markdown syntax into this field via the official Meta Business Suite or third-party connectors like Twilio or MessageBird, the service providers will sanitize the input before it reaches the WhatsApp servers, stripping away any attempt at inline styling. If you are using a platform that supports rich text rendering outside of WhatsApp, such as a custom landing page or an email newsletter, you can implement this behavior by injecting JavaScript listeners that detect selection and copy specific text ranges to the clipboard. This approach relies on the browser's ability to interpret DOM elements, which WhatsApp does not expose in its chat interface. Therefore, any solution claiming to generate inline clickable links inside a standard WhatsApp chat window is likely misrepresenting how the app actually functions or is referring to a custom-built application that uses the WhatsApp Business API for notifications rather than direct chat messages. The core takeaway for technical implementation is that you must work within the boundaries of the platform's data model. To ensure your recipients can easily interact with your content, design your workflow so that the actionable URL is distinct from the informational text. This separation not only works around the formatting restrictions but also improves accessibility, ensuring screen readers and copy-paste utilities can process the link correctly without ambiguity.
